cases.title: fix(gitea): resolve base_url_html on first use so a repo-level web_url applies
cases.description:
`apply_repo_settings()` builds the provider before it merges the repo's
`.pr_agent.toml`, and `GiteaProvider.__init__` resolved `base_url_html` as its
last step, so a repo-level `[gitea] web_url` never reached the links published
in comments. #2617 documented that as a caveat on the `web_url` setting; the
constructor was the wrong place for it, as noted on #2620.

`base_url_html` is now a property, resolved on first use and cached, with a
setter so callers and tests that assign it keep working. Its only readers,
`get_line_link()` and `get_pr_url()`, run after the settings merge. The
`web_url` comment in `configuration.toml` now says the per-repo override
applies.

Tests: the constructor leaves the URL unresolved, a `web_url` that lands after
construction is used by both readers, resolution happens once, and an assigned
value is used as is. The first two fail on `main`.

Closes #3026

tickets.title: [Bug]: Repository-level [ignore] rules are applied too late for Gitea PRs
tickets.body:
### Git provider

Other

### System Info

- PR-Agent image: `pragent/pr-agent:0.41.0-gitea_app`
- Git provider: Gitea
- Trigger: manual `/review`
- Repository settings: enabled

### Bug details

```markdown
### Current behavior

Repository-level `[ignore]` rules from `.pr_agent.toml` are loaded successfully for Gitea pull requests, but they do not exclude matching files from the review diff sent to the model.

The logs show that the repository config is applied:

```text
Applying repo settings (sections: ['ignore', 'pr_reviewer'])
```

However, files matching the configured ignore globs are still present in the subsequent `PR diff` log and are included in the review prompt.

### Expected behavior

When `CONFIG.USE_REPO_SETTINGS_FILE=true` and a repository contains a valid `.pr_agent.toml`, its `[ignore].glob` and `[ignore].regex` rules should exclude matching files from the review analysis.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Run PR-Agent with Gitea and repository settings enabled:

   ```yaml
   CONFIG__USE_REPO_SETTINGS_FILE: "true"
   GITEA__REPO_SETTING: .pr_agent.toml
   ```

2. Add this file to the root of the PR head branch:

   ```toml
   [ignore]
   glob = [
     "generated/**",
     "api/schema.d.ts",
   ]
   regex = []
   ```

3. Open a PR that changes both:

   ```text
   generated/client.py
   api/schema.d.ts
   src/application.py
   ```

4. Trigger `/review`.

### Actual result

`generated/client.py` and `api/schema.d.ts` are still included in the PR diff and review context.

### Suspected cause

In the Gitea flow, `apply_repo_settings(pr_url)` constructs `GiteaProvider` before loading the repository-level `.pr_agent.toml`.

During `GiteaProvider.__init__`, PR files are fetched and immediately passed to:

```python
filter_ignored(self.git_files, platform="gitea")
```

Only afterwards does `apply_repo_settings()` fetch and merge `.pr_agent.toml`. There is no second filtering pass after the repository settings have been applied.

Relevant code:

- `pr_agent/git_providers/gitea_provider.py`
- `pr_agent/git_providers/utils.py`

### Suggested fix

Either:

1. make repository `[ignore]` settings available before the Gitea provider fetches and filters PR files; or
2. re-run `filter_ignored(self.git_files, platform="gitea")` after repository settings are merged and before `get_diff_files()` builds the review payload.

A regression test should verify that a Gitea PR with a repository-level `.pr_agent.toml` excludes files matched by both `ignore.glob` and `ignore.regex`.

tickets.title: Gitea: base_url_html is resolved in the constructor, so a repo-level gitea.web_url never applies
tickets.body:
Follow-on from #2620, where @IsmaelMartinez noted that `GiteaProvider.__init__` still resolves settings-dependent state and suggested this get its own issue. #2617 added `base_url_html` and documented the limitation on the `web_url` setting in `configuration.toml`: "read when the provider is constructed, before repo-level .pr_agent.toml settings are merged, so a per-repo override does not apply to /describe, /review and /improve".

Mechanism: `apply_repo_settings()` (`pr_agent/git_providers/utils.py:257`) constructs the provider through `get_git_provider_with_context()` and only then fetches and merges the repo's `.pr_agent.toml`. `GiteaProvider.__init__` ends with `self.base_url_html = self._resolve_base_url_html()` (`gitea_provider.py:120`), so the user-facing URL is fixed before a repo-level `[gitea] web_url` exists, and every tool that later reuses the cached provider from the request context builds its links from the wrong base.

Fix: resolve `base_url_html` on first use rather than in the constructor. Its only readers are `get_line_link()` and `get_pr_url()`, both called after the settings merge.

cases.title: fix(review): keep the persistent review when the agent identity is unproven
cases.description:
Closes #3071.

## Description

`persistent_comment` (default `true`) promises that "every new review request will edit the previous one".
Since #2722 the reviewer refuses to touch a review comment unless the provider can *prove* PR-Agent authored
it, and demotes the result to a `## Standalone PR Review` comment otherwise. In three ordinary deployments the
identity is merely *unresolved* rather than *foreign*, so the promise is broken on every run.

### Root cause

`PRReviewer.run()` reaches the demotion whenever `_review_finding_state_in_play()` is true (any provider that
overrides `supports_review_finding_state`) but `_review_comment_authorship_available()` is false:

| Trigger | Why the identity is unknown |
|---|---|
| GitHub App, any automatic command (`pr_commands`, `push_commands`, `review_commands`) | In app mode the login was only ever cached by `publish_comment`, i.e. by the *"Preparing review…"* progress comment — which `config.is_auto_command` suppresses. |
| GitHub Actions, every rerun | `deployment_type=user` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`; `GET /user` answers 403 *"Resource not accessible by integration"*, so `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent` raises and the run is treated as a provider read failure. |
| Azure DevOps, shipped configuration | `supports_review_finding_state()` is `bool(_configured_stable_agent_identities())` and `configuration.toml` ships `agent_identity = ""`. |
| Any provider, when one key issue lacks a file or body | `_review_findings_from_data` returned `None` for the whole collection, blocking the state and demoting the review. |

### The fix

Three changes, each addressing one link in that chain:

1. **`github_provider.py` — resolve the identity instead of giving up.** App deployments read their own
   `<slug>[bot]` login from the app JWT (`GithubIntegration.get_app()`), which does not depend on having
   commented before. User deployments that cannot call `GET /user` fall back to `github-actions[bot]` when
   `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, which is the login the workflow token posts as.
2. **`pr_reviewer.py` — separate creating from updating.** When no comment carries the full-review identity,
   creating one cannot overwrite a comment PR-Agent did not author, so the review is published persistently.
   The demotion is kept for the case it was written for: a comment already exists and authorship is unproven.
3. **`pr_reviewer.py` — drop an untrackable key issue instead of the whole collection.** A finding with no
   file or body is skipped for lifecycle purposes and still rendered in the summary. Because a dropped
   finding is not an absent one, that run is barred from resolving anything.

## Behaviour change

| Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| App auto command, fresh PR | new `## Standalone PR Review` comment each run | the persistent review, created once and edited afterwards |
| Actions rerun | a second standalone comment per run | the previous review is edited in place |
| Azure DevOps, default config | standalone comment | persistent review |
| One fileless key issue | whole review demoted, state frozen | review updated, that one finding not tracked |
| **Comment exists, authorship unproven (forged marker)** | standalone comment, original untouched | **unchanged** |
| Provider comments unreadable | standalone comment | **unchanged** (cannot know what it would replace) |

## Testing

```
$ PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/unittest
3694 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 94 warnings in 58.24s
```

New file `tests/unittest/test_review_persistent_comment_authorship.py` (9 tests), each written first and
proven to fail without the fix (8 failed / 1 passed before, 9 passed after). It drives the real
`PRReviewer.run()` against a real `GithubProvider` and a real `AzureDevopsProvider`; only the PyGithub client,
the diff and the model are faked. It covers the four triggers, a resolvable-identity control, and two
security edge cases:

- `test_forged_review_comment_is_never_edited` — a human-authored comment carrying the identity marker is
  left untouched and the result is still a standalone comment.
- `test_unreadable_comments_do_not_create_a_second_review` — a provider read failure stays conservative.

The pre-existing authorship tests in `tests/unittest/test_pr_reviewer_finding_state.py`, including
`test_review_run_does_not_edit_forged_persistent_comment_without_authorship`, pass unchanged.

Also checked: `ruff check` clean on every file touched.

## Risk / compatibility

The forgery protection introduced by #2722 is preserved exactly: the only newly-allowed write is *creating*
a comment when none exists. Deployments that already resolved their identity take the same path as before.
`GithubIntegration.get_app()` is called at most once per provider instance and only in app mode; any failure
is logged and degrades to the previous behaviour.

tickets.title: fix(review): keep the persistent review when the agent identity is unproven
tickets.body:
### Git provider

Other

### System Info

- **PR-Agent version:** 0.45.0, branch `main` (commit `ab888b90`)
- **Python:** 3.12.14
- **Deployment type:** app (automatic commands), action (every rerun), cli/app for Azure DevOps
- **Model:** any (the defect is independent of the model)


### Bug details

`/review` stops maintaining its persistent review comment and posts a new
**"Standalone PR Review"** comment instead, carrying the notice *"PR-Agent could not safely update the
persistent review. This standalone result will not replace the canonical review."*

Because that comment deliberately carries no identity marker, the next run does not find it either, so the
comments accumulate — one per review — and the documented behaviour of `persistent_comment` (*"every new
review request will edit the previous one"*) never happens.

It reproduces in three ordinary deployments, none of which involve a foreign comment:

1. **GitHub App running any automatic command** (`pr_commands` on PR open, `push_commands`,
   `review_commands`). Automatic commands set `config.is_auto_command`, which suppresses the
   *"Preparing review…"* progress comment. That progress comment was the only thing that taught the provider
   its own bot login, so `supports_review_finding_state()` returns `False` and the review is demoted.
2. **GitHub Actions, every rerun.** The runner sets `deployment_type=user` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
   `is_comment_authored_by_pr_agent` calls `GET /user`, which an installation token may not use — GitHub
   answers `403 Resource not accessible by integration` — so the run is treated as a provider read failure.
3. **Azure DevOps with the shipped configuration.** `supports_review_finding_state()` is
   `bool(_configured_stable_agent_identities())` and `configuration.toml` ships `agent_identity = ""`.
   The setting is presented as optional in `docs/docs/installation/azure.md`.

A fourth, provider-independent trigger: if the model returns one key issue without a `relevant_file` or with
an empty `issue_content`, `_review_findings_from_data` discards the entire collection and the same demotion
happens, even though the review summary renders that finding fine.

### Reproduction

Minimal case (GitHub App, automatic command, fresh PR):

1. Install PR-Agent as a GitHub App with the default `github_app.pr_commands`.
2. Open a pull request.
3. Push a second commit so `push_commands` runs again.

**Expected:** one persistent review comment, edited on the second run.
**Actual:** two `## Standalone PR Review` comments, neither of which is the canonical review.

An executable reproduction driving the real `PRReviewer.run()` against a real `GithubProvider` is in
`tests/unittest/test_review_persistent_comment_authorship.py` on the accompanying branch; on `ab888b90` it
reports 8 failed / 1 passed.

cases.title: feat(tickets): make the shorthand issue-number bound configurable
cases.description:
Implements #3081.

## Description

`extract_ticket_links_from_pr_description` follows a bare `#123` reference only while it has
fewer than five digits. That bound is deliberate — `tests/unittest/test_markdown_ticket_output_core.py`
pins it with `test_hash_only_rejects_long_numbers`, commented *"5 digits, looks like a code, not an
issue"* — and it is right for most repositories.

It is wrong for a repository whose issue numbers have outgrown it. Once a project passes its
10 000th issue, the standard `Fixes #12345` closing keyword stops being recognised, so ticket
compliance (`require_ticket_analysis_review`, on by default) silently never runs. Nothing is logged.

### The change

The bound becomes a setting rather than a constant:

```toml
[config]
max_shorthand_issue_digits = 4   # unchanged default
```

`get_max_shorthand_issue_digits()` reads it, coerces a string (environment overrides arrive as
strings), and falls back to the default with a warning when the value is unusable or non-positive.

Unambiguous forms are untouched, because they were never bounded: a full issue URL and the
cross-repository `owner/repo#123` shorthand both name their repository explicitly.

## Behaviour change

| Description | Default | `max_shorthand_issue_digits = 7` |
|---|---|---|
| `Fixes #1234` | followed | followed |
| `Fixes #12345` | ignored (unchanged) | followed |
| `Fixes https://github.com/org/repo/issues/1234567` | followed | followed |
| `Fixes other/project#12345` | followed | followed |

Nothing changes unless an operator raises the bound.

## Testing

```
$ PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/unittest
3703 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 91 warnings in 50.61s
```

New file `tests/unittest/test_github_issue_reference_extraction.py` (18 tests), written first.
Covers the unchanged default, a raised bound, a bound that still excludes longer numbers, five
unusable configuration values, a numeric string, and the two unambiguous forms as controls.

`test_hash_only_rejects_long_numbers` in the existing suite passes unchanged, which is the point:
the default behaviour the maintainers chose is preserved exactly.

Also checked: `ruff check` clean on both files.

## Risk / compatibility

Default-preserving by construction. The only new failure mode — a bad configured value — falls back
to the default and warns.

## Note on provenance

This started as a bug report ("five-digit issue references are never extracted"). The existing test
above shows the bound is an intentional product decision, so it is offered as opt-in configurability
rather than a behaviour change. The corresponding entry in `BUG_REPORT_ROUND4.md` has been withdrawn.

tickets.title: feat(tickets): make the shorthand issue-number bound configurable
tickets.body:
### Feature request

Make the digit bound on bare `#123` issue references configurable, so repositories with more
than 9 999 issues keep their ticket compliance.

`pr_agent/tools/ticket_pr_compliance_check.py::extract_ticket_links_from_pr_description` follows
a shorthand reference only when `len(issue_number) < 5`:

```python
else:  # #123 format
    issue_number = match[5][1:]
    if issue_number.isdigit() and len(issue_number) < 5 and repo_path:
        _add(...)
```

The bound is intentional — `test_hash_only_rejects_long_numbers` pins it, on the grounds that a
bare five-digit number looks more like an error code than an issue — and it is a reasonable
default. But it is a global constant, so a project that has passed its 10 000th issue has no way
to opt out.

For those repositories the effect is silent: `Fixes #12345` is matched by the pattern and then
discarded, nothing is logged, and `require_ticket_analysis_review` (on by default) simply never
finds a ticket. The neighbouring branch-name extractor already accepts up to six digits
(`BRANCH_ISSUE_PATTERN`), and the full-URL form has no bound at all, so the four-digit ceiling is
also inconsistent within the same module.


### Motivation


### Proposed behaviour

```toml
[config]
max_shorthand_issue_digits = 4   # default: today's behaviour
```

- unset or unusable → today's behaviour, with a warning for an unusable value;
- raised → longer shorthand references are followed;
- full URLs and `owner/repo#123` stay unbounded, since they name their repository.

### Alternatives considered

- **Always allow up to 7 digits.** Rejected: it overrides a maintainer decision that a bare long
  number is probably not an issue, and it breaks an existing test that documents the intent.
- **Allow long numbers only after a closing keyword** (`Fixes`, `Closes`, …). Rejected for the same
  reason: the existing test uses `Fixes #12345` and still expects it to be ignored.

cases.title: fix(github): report command failures in outcome reactions
cases.description:
## Summary

Fix GitHub outcome reactions reporting success after a PR-Agent tool failed.

## Root cause

The GitHub comment handler uses the boolean returned by `PRAgent.handle_request()` to select the configured outcome reaction.

Review, description, and code-suggestion tools can catch internal provider/model errors and return normally when `config.propagate_tool_errors = false`, which is the shipped compatibility default. The handler therefore receives `True` and adds `reaction_on_success` even though the command failed.

The existing reaction tests only used fake agents that directly returned `True` or `False`; they did not cover the real Agent/tool error contract.

## Changes

- Add an optional request-scoped `propagate_tool_errors` override to `PRAgent.handle_request()`.
- Pass the override through the Agent routing path and apply it after repository and command settings are processed.
- Restore the previous setting in `finally`.
- Enable the override for GitHub comment commands whose result is consumed by `react_to_outcome()`.
- Add a regression using a provider-free tool that reproduces the existing swallow/propagate behavior.

The shipped default behavior for callers that do not pass the override is unchanged.

## Validation

- Baseline regression: `1 failed, 34 deselected`
- Fixed regression: `1 passed, 34 deselected`
- Reaction tests: `35 passed`
- Full unittest suite: `4338 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed`
- Ruff: passed
- compileall: passed
- pre-commit: passed
- Package sdist/wheel build: passed
- Docker `--target test` build: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

These are local Docker-based results. No live provider, external CI, deployment, or production result is claimed.

cases.title: fix(github): report total inline suggestion fallback failure
cases.description:
# Title

fix(github): report total inline suggestion fallback failure

# Description

Fixes #3223

## Summary

Fix GitHub code-suggestion publication reporting when the initial batch review fails with HTTP 422 and the verification fallback drops every comment.

Previously, `GithubProvider.publish_code_suggestions()` returned `True` whenever `publish_inline_comments()` completed without raising, even if the 422 fallback ultimately published zero comments. This caused `PRCodeSuggestions` to treat the run as successful and skip its existing retry path.

## Changes

* Track the number of comments actually published by `_publish_inline_comments_fallback_with_verification()`.
* Return `False` when the 422 fallback publishes zero comments.
* Preserve `True` for partial fallback success to avoid duplicate retries of suggestions that already landed.
* Preserve successful no-op behavior for persistent inline-comment dedup when all suggestions were already posted.
* Make `publish_code_suggestions()` return the actual result from `publish_inline_comments()` instead of unconditionally returning `True`.
* Add regression tests covering total fallback failure, partial success, repaired-comment success/failure, normal success, and persistent dedup-only behavior.

## Scope

This change is intentionally limited to the GitHub provider.

It does not modify:

* GitLab or other providers
* the caller retry policy in `PRCodeSuggestions`
* pre-submission validation/drop semantics
* provider-wide publication contracts

## Validation

* `tests/unittest/test_github_provider_comments.py`: 39 passed
* `tests/unittest/test_inline_comment_dedup.py`: 41 passed
* GitHub fallback verification tests: 4 passed
* Relevant PR code-suggestion tests: 170 passed
* Ruff: passed
* Pre-commit: passed
* `git diff --check`: clean

tickets.title: GitHub publish_code_suggestions reports success when the 422 fallback drops every comment
tickets.body:
### Summary

`GithubProvider.publish_code_suggestions` returns `True` when the 422 fallback path drops **every** comment, so a run in which nothing was posted is reported to the caller as a successful publication.

This is the same invariant as #3109 (GitLab) and the one #3117 tracks, but on the reference provider. Gitea (#2878), Bitbucket (#2992), and Bitbucket Server already count publishable-vs-published; GitHub does not.

### Where

`pr_agent/git_providers/github_provider.py`:

```python
try:
    self.publish_inline_comments(post_parameters_list)
    return True
except Exception as e:
    get_logger().error(f"Failed to publish code suggestion, error: {e}")
    return False
```

`publish_inline_comments` returns `None` on every non-raising path, so `return True` is unconditional whenever it does not raise. On a 422 it calls `_publish_inline_comments_fallback_with_verification`, which:

- posts only `verified_comments` (may be empty),
- and, when `_try_fix_invalid_inline_comments` fixes nothing, logs
  `Dropped N invalid comments that could not be fixed` and returns normally.

Nothing was posted; the caller is told it succeeded.

### Why it matters

`pr_agent/tools/pr_code_suggestions.py` reads the return value as the failure signal:

```python
is_successful = self.git_provider.publish_code_suggestions(code_suggestions)
if is_successful:
    self._output_published = True
if not is_successful:
    # retry each suggestion separately
```

So the one-by-one retry — which exists precisely to salvage suggestions the batch review rejected — is suppressed exactly in the case it was written for, and `_output_published` is set for output that does not exist.

### Reproduction

```python
from unittest.mock import MagicMock
from pr_agent.git_providers.github_provider import GithubProvider

p = GithubProvider.__new__(GithubProvider)
p.pr = MagicMock()
p.last_commit_id = "abc"
p.max_comment_chars = None
p.validate_comments_inside_hunks = lambda s: s

err = Exception("unprocessable"); err.status = 422
p.pr.create_review.side_effect = err
# every comment fails verification, none can be fixed
p._verify_code_comments = lambda comments: ([], [(c, "bad") for c in comments])
p._try_fix_invalid_inline_comments = lambda comments: []

suggestions = [{
    "body": "x\n```suggestion\ny\n```",
    "relevant_file": "app.py",
    "relevant_lines_start": 1,
    "relevant_lines_end": 1,
}]
assert p.publish_code_suggestions(suggestions) is False
```

Observed on `main` (`9b7bb8cd`):

```
AssertionError: assert True is False
 +  where True = publish_code_suggestions([...])
--- Captured stderr ---
INFO  ... Initially failed to publish inline comments as committable
WARNING ... Dropped 1 invalid comments that could not be fixed. Paths: ['app.py']
```

### Suggested fix

Make `publish_inline_comments` (and its fallback) report how many comments actually landed, and have `publish_code_suggestions` return the shape already merged elsewhere:

```python
return published_count > 0 or publishable_count == 0
```

Two behaviours must be preserved, and both already have precedent in the merged providers:

- **Partial failure must still return `True`** — the caller republishes the whole list, which would duplicate the suggestions that did land.
- **The persistent-dedup early return must stay `True`.** When `config.persistent_inline_comments` is on and every suggestion was already posted on an earlier run, `publish_inline_comments` returns early with `Persistent inline comments: all N suggestion(s) already posted; nothing to publish`. Nothing was published *this* run, but nothing needed to be — this is `publishable_count == 0`, not a failure. I confirmed this path currently returns `True` and it should keep doing so; a naive `published_count > 0` would regress it into an infinite one-by-one retry of comments that are already on the PR.

### Scope

I am not opening a PR for this yet — #3219 (Gerrit + CodeCommit) is awaiting review and #3129 owns the GitLab half (#3109), so this is the remaining provider. Happy to take it if a maintainer wants it, either as its own change or folded into whichever of those lands first.

cases.title: fix(providers): make the base persistent comment actually persist
cases.description:
Fixes #3181.

## What was wrong

`GitProvider.publish_persistent_comment` did not persist anything — it called `publish_comment`. The real implementation is `publish_persistent_comment_full` directly below it. Five providers overrode the base only to forward to it, and the four that never overrode it (codecommit, gerrit, local, plain-diff) got no persistence at all.

## Changes

- **The base delegates to `publish_persistent_comment_full`**, so providers that never overrode it inherit persistence instead of duplicating a comment on every rerun.
- **Removed the five pure pass-through overrides** — `gitlab_provider.py`, `gitea_provider.py`, `bitbucket_provider.py`, `bitbucket_server_provider.py`, `azuredevops_provider.py`. Each was read before deletion and none carried behaviour beyond the forward. `GithubProvider` keeps its override: it has a real check-run branch.
- **Aligned the signature drift.** `as_thread` was accepted by the base, gitlab and bitbucket-server but not by github, so the next provider to return `True` from `should_publish_review_as_thread()` would have hit a `TypeError`. `GithubProvider.publish_persistent_comment` now accepts and forwards it.
- **Dropped the `publisher.__func__ is GitProvider.publish_persistent_comment` check** in `pr_reviewer.py:465`. It existed only to detect the non-persisting base, and it is exactly the provider-type branching AGENTS.md tells us to avoid. The capability gate below it (`supports_review_finding_state()` + `is_supported("get_issue_comments")`) already covers the case correctly.

## One thing the issue did not mention

Delegating unconditionally introduces a silent data-loss bug, so this PR adds `GitProvider.supports_comment_editing()` to guard it.

The base `edit_comment` is a no-op returning `None`, and `publish_persistent_comment_full` only treats `False` as an edit failure. Gerrit reports `get_issue_comments` as supported (`gerrit_provider.py:356` leaves it commented out of the unsupported list) but never implemented `edit_comment`. With an unguarded delegation it would match an existing comment, no-op the edit, and then publish only the `**[Persistent review](...)** updated to latest commit ...` status line — **the review body would never reach the PR**.

I reproduced this against a fake provider mirroring gerrit's shape before adding the guard: the only published call was the status line. Providers that cannot edit now create a new comment instead, which is the pre-existing behaviour for them. The regression test fails if the guard is removed.

## Coordination

Deliberately does not touch `codecommit_provider.py` or `codecommit_client.py`, so this does not conflict with the open #3158. #3155 has already merged.

## Tests

Added coverage for: the base updating a matching comment; the base falling back to `publish_comment` when none matches; a provider without `edit_comment` publishing the body rather than losing it; `CodeCommitProvider`/`LocalGitProvider` inheriting the implementation; and `GithubProvider` forwarding `as_thread`.

```
PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest tests/unittest -q
4461 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed in 99.51s
```

`uv run ruff check` clean on every touched file.

tickets.title: Base publish_persistent_comment does not persist; four provider overrides are pure pass-throughs
tickets.body:
`GitProvider.publish_persistent_comment` does not persist anything, and most providers override it only to undo that.

Verified on `main` (6275ac09):

- The base at `pr_agent/git_providers/git_provider.py:524` just calls `publish_comment`. The real implementation is `publish_persistent_comment_full` immediately below it.
- Four of the six overrides are pure pass-throughs to `publish_persistent_comment_full` adding no behaviour: `gitlab_provider.py:942`, `gitea_provider.py:325`, `bitbucket_server_provider.py:356`, `azuredevops_provider.py:979`. GitHub adds only a check-run branch before delegating.
- Four providers never override it, so they get no persistence at all: `codecommit_provider.py`, `gerrit_provider.py`, `local_git_provider.py`, `plain_diff_provider.py`.
- `pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py:465` has to detect this by comparing `publisher.__func__ is GitProvider.publish_persistent_comment`, which is exactly the provider-type branching AGENTS.md tells us to avoid.

This is the shared root cause behind #3157 (CodeCommit duplicates comments on rerun) and #3145 (Bitbucket Cloud diverges), both currently being patched per provider in #3158 and #3155.

Also worth fixing in the same pass: the override signatures have drifted. `as_thread` is accepted by the base, gitlab and bitbucket_server, but not by github, gitea, bitbucket or azuredevops. That is safe today only because GitLab is the sole provider returning `True` from `should_publish_review_as_thread()`, so the next provider to opt in hits a `TypeError`.

Suggested action: make the base delegate to `publish_persistent_comment_full`, delete the four redundant overrides, align the signatures, and drop the `__func__` check. Please coordinate with #3155 and #3158 first so we do not conflict.

tickets.body:
## Summary

`docs/docs/tools/review.md:220` (live at https://docs.pr-agent.ai/tools/review/) documents auto-generated PR labels including a `ticket compliance` label and two configuration flags that do not exist anywhere in the code or in `pr_agent/settings/configuration.toml`. It also names `Linea` as a ticket system that is not supported.

## Evidence

The doc claims:

> **`ticket compliance`**: Adds a label ... to any GitHub/Jira/Linea ticket linked in the PR. Controlled by the `require_ticket_labels` flag (default: false). If `require_no_ticket_labels` is also enabled, PRs without ticket links will receive a "No ticket found" label.

- `git grep "require_ticket_labels|require_no_ticket_labels"` matches only this docs file - the keys do not exist in code or `configuration.toml`.
- The only labels the review tool actually publishes are `Review effort X/5` and `Possible security concern` (`set_review_labels`, `pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py:1246-1298`).
- Ticket compliance levels ("Fully compliant", "Partially compliant", "Not compliant") are rendered as text inside the review comment by `ticket_markdown_logic` (`pr_agent/algo/utils.py:571+`), never published as PR labels.
- "Linea" is not a supported ticket system anywhere; the ticket pipeline covers GitHub issues, GitLab issues, Jira Cloud, and Asana (`pr_agent/tools/ticket_pr_compliance_check.py`).

## Impact

Users following the docs expect a label that the tool never applies, and may set `require_ticket_labels`/`require_no_ticket_labels` in config expecting an effect. At minimum the documented behavior should be removed or replaced with what actually happens.

## Expected

Drop the `ticket compliance` bullet (and the `Linea` reference) from review.md, or update it to describe the real behavior.

tickets.title: security: clone persists GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea tokens in .git/config
tickets.body:
### Git provider

GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea

### Bug details

The GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea providers embed access tokens directly into clone URLs in `_prepare_clone_url_with_token()`. The shared `GitProvider.clone()` then invokes `git clone` with that authenticated URL.

Git persists the remote URL in the new checkout's `.git/config`, leaving the token in plaintext on disk:

```text
[remote "origin"]
    url = https://<token>@host/owner/repository.git
```

This affects temporary review checkouts and can expose credentials through filesystem snapshots, backups, container volume mounts, diagnostics, or any process that can read the checkout directory. The token may grant repository read or write access depending on its scope.

### Reproduction

1. Configure a GitHub, GitLab, or Gitea provider with a personal or access token.
2. Trigger a command that clones the repository (for example, repository documentation/context loading).
3. Before the temporary checkout is removed, inspect its Git configuration:

```bash
git -C <clone-directory> config --get remote.origin.url
cat <clone-directory>/.git/config
```

The output contains the access token embedded in the remote URL.

### Expected behavior

Access tokens should not be persisted in `.git/config` or any clone metadata. Authentication should be supplied per Git operation through a protected credential helper or temporary configuration that is removed after the operation, while the origin URL remains token-free.

### Suggested remediation

- Keep the repository URL token-free.
- Provide authentication through a mode-600 temporary credential helper/configuration scoped to the clone/fetch operation.
- Ensure cleanup happens on success, failure, and timeout.
- Add regression tests asserting that the resulting `.git/config` and `remote.origin.url` contain no token.

cases.title: fix(review): keep findings with non-numeric line fields
cases.description:
Fixes #3589

## Problem

`convert_to_markdown_v2` (`pr_agent/algo/utils.py:318-319`) called `int(str(issue.get("start_line", 0)).strip())` inside a per-finding `try/except Exception`. When the model emitted a non-integer line field (empty string, `N/A`, a float, `null`, or a hyphenated range), the `ValueError` was caught and the entire finding was dropped from the published `/review` summary with no user-visible error.

The two sibling consumers of the same dict are tolerant and keep the finding:

- `pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py:1263-1266` (`_build_key_issue_comment`), inline comments.
- `pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py:648-651` (`_review_finding_from_issue`), persisted finding state.

So a "Possible security issue" could vanish from the summary while inline comments and the persistent state still recorded it, and the bookkeeping for later reviews diverged from what maintainers actually saw.

## Fix

In `convert_to_markdown_v2`, parse `start_line`/`end_line` tolerantly (defaulting to `0` on non-numeric input, matching the sibling paths). When the lines are not usable (`start_line < 1` or `end_line < start_line`), the finding still renders in the summary with its header and content, but without a line anchor link or excerpt. Calling `extract_relevant_lines_str` and `get_line_link` is gated on `valid_lines` so no bogus `R0` anchor is produced.

## Tests

Added `test_key_issue_with_non_numeric_lines_keeps_finding_in_summary` in `tests/unittest/test_convert_to_markdown.py`: a finding with `start_line: ""` still renders header and content and `get_line_link` is not called.

Verification:

- New test plus the reviewer, finding-state, and markdown render suites pass.
- Full unit suite: 9187 passed, 33 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- `ruff check` and the pre-commit hooks are clean on the touched files.

tickets.title: review: a non-numeric start_line or end_line silently drops the finding from the published summary while inline comments and persisted state keep it
tickets.body:
### Git provider
All (provider-independent; lives in `pr_agent/algo/utils.py`)

### System Info
- Tool: PR-Agent, `/review` command, any deployment
- Default configuration

### Bug details

A key review finding silently disappears from the published `/review` summary whenever the model emits a non-integer value for `start_line` or `end_line`. The finding (header, content, file link) is dropped from the review with no user-visible error, while two sibling code paths keep it, so the review bookkeeping diverges from what maintainers actually see.

`convert_to_markdown_v2` builds the "Recommended focus areas for review" section at `pr_agent/algo/utils.py:318-319`:

```python
start_line = int(str(issue.get('start_line', 0)).strip())
end_line = int(str(issue.get('end_line', 0)).strip())
```

A value that is not int-coercible, for example `""`, `"N/A"`, `12.5`, or `null` (which becomes the string `"None"`), raises `ValueError`. The whole per-issue block is wrapped in `try`/`except Exception` at `pr_agent/algo/utils.py:305-342`, so the exception is logged (`get_logger().exception(...)`) and the entire finding is dropped from the summary.

The two other consumers of the exact same dict tolerate this input intentionally and keep the finding:

- `pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py:1263-1266` (`_build_key_issue_comment`): `except ValueError: start_line, end_line = 0, 0`, comment still published inline.
- `pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py:648-651` (`_review_finding_from_issue`): `except (TypeError, ValueError): start, end = 0, 0`, finding still recorded in the persistent finding state, which later incremental reviews and inline-comment resolution use.

So a "Possible security issue" or similar key finding can be dropped from the summary while the tool still records it as a known/resolved finding, and inline comments can carry it. Summary output, inline output, and persisted state disagree about the same review.

Reproduction (feeds same shape the model returns after YAML load):

```python
from pr_agent.algo.utils import convert_to_markdown_v2

data = {"review": {"key_issues_to_review": [{
    "relevant_file": "src/foo.py",
    "issue_header": "Possible security issue",
    "issue_content": "Credentials are logged on the error path.",
    "start_line": "",   # or "N/A", 12.5, null
    "end_line": 14,
}]}}

markdown = convert_to_markdown_v2(data)   # "Possible security issue" is absent
```

With integer fields the finding renders; with a non-integer `start_line` or `end_line` it disappears. The negative cases are realistic model outputs: empty string, float, `null`, or a hyphenated range such as `"12-15"`.

Suggested fix: reuse the tolerant parsing already present in `pr_reviewer.py`, defaulting non-numeric lines to `0`, so the finding still renders with header and content (matching the sibling paths), or drop it from the state everywhere consistently. No existing unit test asserts the current drop behavior.

cases.title: fix(diff): keep all hunks spanned by a line range
cases.description:
## Problem

`extract_hunk_lines_from_patch()` decides whether a hunk participates in a requested line range by checking only `line_start` against each hunk's span. When `line_end` reaches into a later hunk, that later hunk is skipped entirely and its lines silently disappear from `selected_lines`.

This is the fallback used by `extract_relevant_lines_str()` when `file.head_file` is missing, and by `/ask` line questions in `pr_line_questions.py`. A range that crosses a hunk boundary returns truncated context, so the model never sees the later lines.

Example: with hunks covering new lines 1..4 and 11..13, requesting lines 2..12 returns only lines 2,3,4. The lines 11,12 are dropped with no warning.

## Fix

Gate each hunk on whether the requested range overlaps it:

- Left side: keep the hunk when `line_end >= start1` and `line_start <= start1 + size1 - 1`.
- Right side: keep the hunk when `line_end >= start2` and `line_start <= start2 + size2 - 1`.

Single hunk behavior is unchanged; all existing tests still pass.

## Tests

Added right and left side cases where the range spans both hunks, asserting both hunk headers are present and selected lines come from both hunks.

Full unit suite: 9353 passed.

cases.title: fix(tokens): avoid a stale cached encoder on concurrent model switch
cases.description:
## Problem

`TokenEncoder` caches one tokenizer for the whole process, together with the model that tokenizer belongs to. `get_token_encoder` checked that pair outside the lock and published `_model` before the tokenizer finished building:

```python
if cls._encoder_instance is None or model != cls._model:  # no lock
    with cls._lock:
        if cls._encoder_instance is None or model != cls._model:
            cls._model = model                                   # published first
            cls._encoder_instance = cls._create_encoder(cls._model)  # slow, published second
return cls._encoder_instance
```

While a tokenizer is being built, `_model` already names the new model but `_encoder_instance` still holds the previous model's tokenizer. A concurrent request for the new model sees `_encoder_instance is not None` and `model == cls._model`, concludes the cache is warm, skips the lock, and is handed the previous model's tokenizer.

Tokenizer construction is slow, especially on first use of a model, so the window is wide enough to hit in the webhook server where several PRs are processed at once.

The result is silent wrong token counts. `TokenHandler` uses them to decide how much of a diff fits in the context window, so a request can be trimmed against the wrong model's vocabulary and still overflow, or be trimmed far more aggressively than needed.

## Fix

Do the check and the build in one critical section, and publish `_model` only once its tokenizer exists:

```python
with cls._lock:
    if cls._encoder_instance is None or model != cls._model:
        encoder = cls._create_encoder(model)
        cls._model = model
        cls._encoder_instance = encoder
return cls._encoder_instance
```

A concurrent caller now blocks on the lock and then reads a cache that is consistent, so every caller gets the tokenizer for the model it asked for.

The lock-free fast path is dropped. It was the source of the inconsistency, and `get_token_encoder` is called only a handful of times per request, so an uncontended acquire is not measurable next to the `encode` work that follows. Building under the lock is unchanged, since the original code already built there.

## Test

`test_concurrent_model_switch_does_not_hand_out_previous_model_encoder` starts a model switch with a slow encoder build, then makes a concurrent call for the same model and asserts both callers receive the same new encoder rather than the stale one.

It fails on the previous implementation and passes on this one. Verified both ways: the cache invariant check and the stale-encoder symptom check each fail when the old code is restored.

## Scope

Two files, one issue. No changes to encoder selection, model fallback, or the `model != configured_model` path.

tickets.title: Bitbucket Cloud line links break for filenames with a space or #
tickets.body:
`BitbucketProvider.get_line_link` (`bitbucket_provider.py:544-549`) puts the raw filename into the `#L{file}T{line}` fragment. `docs/my notes.md` gives `.../#Ldocs/my notes.mdT12`, and because Bitbucket Cloud uses the plain `[file](link)` form, the rendered link stops at `#Ldocs/my`. cases.title: fix(review): log all schema validation errors and run require checks (#3973)
cases.description:
## Summary

Fixes #3973.

In `PRReviewer._validate_review_schema` (`pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py`):
- Previously, `except ValidationError as error` logged only `error.errors()[0]` and returned `False` immediately.
- This caused observability gaps:
  1. If Pydantic reported multiple validation errors (e.g. unexpected extra keys under `extra="forbid"` and invalid field types or missing fields), only the first error was logged while the remaining errors were hidden.
  2. Because it returned early on `ValidationError`, the `require_*` checks (e.g. `require_score`, `require_tests`, etc.) never executed if Pydantic validation failed, meaning missing required fields were masked by unknown keys.
  3. When multiple `require_*` settings were enabled and missing from the output, the loop exited on the first missing field (`return False`), hiding subsequent missing required fields.

## Changes

- Iterate over all errors in `error.errors()` and log a warning for each error.
- Do not return early on `ValidationError`; continue to evaluate all `require_*` fields.
- Iterate through all `required_fields` without early exit so every missing required field is logged.
- Return `is_valid` representing overall validation status.

## Testing

- Added unit tests in `tests/unittest/test_pr_reviewer_core.py`:
  - `test_review_schema_logs_all_pydantic_validation_errors`: verifies that all Pydantic errors are logged when multiple validation failures occur.
  - `test_review_schema_runs_require_checks_when_pydantic_validation_fails`: verifies that `require_*` checks run and log missing required fields even when Pydantic validation fails.
  - `test_review_schema_logs_all_missing_required_fields`: verifies that all missing required fields are logged when multiple are missing.
- All 186 reviewer unit tests pass (`uv run pytest tests/unittest/test_pr_reviewer*.py`).
- `uv run ruff check` passes with 0 violations.

cases.title: perf(routing): count diff hunks only when needed
cases.description:
## Summary

Avoid unnecessary diff hunk counting when model-routing rules can be evaluated without scanning patches.

- Check file-count limits and Azure deployment eligibility before counting hunks.
- Compute the hunk count lazily, at most once, only when an eligible rule requires it.
- Preserve routing decisions, rule ordering, and deployment selection.
- Avoid forcing a hunk scan solely for logging.

## Motivation

`count_hunks()` scans and splits patch contents even when routing rules cannot match. Skipping unnecessary scans reduces CPU work and temporary memory allocations, particularly for large diffs.

## Tests

Add regression coverage for file-only rules, file-count and deployment-ineligible rules, multiple hunk-limited rules, zero-hunk results, and invalid rules.

Routing decisions remain unchanged. Missing Azure deployment warnings may be emitted earlier for rules that would otherwise fail a hunk limit.

cases.title: fix(gerrit): reset local edits after failed patch uploads
cases.description:
A failed Gerrit suggestion upload can leave temporary repository edits behind because cleanup only runs after a successful upload.

Attempt cleanup whether the upload succeeds or fails. If both operations fail, preserve the original upload error and log the cleanup failure. If cleanup fails after a successful upload, propagate that failure before publishing the suggestion comment.

cases.title: fix(diff): keep unreadable file notices in chunked diffs
cases.description:
## Problem

When a provider cannot fetch a changed file's contents, PR-Agent marks it with `content_fetch_failed=True` and leaves its patch empty.

Extended and compressed diffs already preserve these failures as manual-review notices. However, fresh multi-diff packing skips empty patches when the full diff exceeds the token budget, causing unreadable files to disappear from both the model input and remaining-file coverage.

## Changes

- Preserve unreadable-file notices in chunked diffs using the existing `_unreadable_file_notice()` helper.
- Carry the failure marker through fresh and prepared diff data.
- Prevent oversized notices from being clipped into incomplete warnings. Instead, report those files as unprocessed.
- Preserve existing behavior for normal empty patches, deleted files, and token budgeting.

## Tests

Added parameterized regression tests covering:

- Full and chunked diffs with line numbers enabled and disabled.
- Mixed readable and unreadable files.
- Multiple unreadable files.
- Insufficient token budgets and `skip`/`clip` policies.
- Prepared-diff reuse.
- Normal empty patches and deleted files.

No new dependencies or configuration changes.

cases.title: fix(review): resolve findings in a chunked review when none were cut
cases.description:
Refs #4136.

This implements the part of the hybrid from the thread that is not in doubt: a chunked `/review` keeps finding resolution on when no finding was left out. Rule used: resolution is blocked only if a finding may be missing from the merged list, that is, a chunk reported `num_max_findings` findings on its own, or the union of the chunks was longer than the limit and the merge cut it. Chunks of two and one findings with a limit of three now resolve fixed findings; the merged list reaching the limit no longer blocks it.

Published output is unchanged (still capped at `num_max_findings` by #4138). `findings_may_be_cut()` in `review_merge.py` computes the flag from the chunk outputs, `_merge_cached_review_chunks` stores it, and `_prepare_review_finding_state` uses it in place of `len(current_findings) < max_findings` for chunked reviews. Single-call reviews keep the old test.

Left open: when findings were cut, resolution stays off, as today. Reconciling state against the uncapped list in that case (state and output using different lists) is not part of this PR; it needs a decision on what "cut" findings should do to previously reported ones.

Tests: `test_review_chunk_merge.py` covers the flag (2+1 with limit 3 is not cut, a full chunk and a merge cut are, repeated findings do not count). `test_pr_reviewer_finding_state.py` runs real chunked results through the merge and the state step: 2+1 resolves a fixed finding, 3+0 and 2+2 do not. The 2+1 test fails without the source change. Full unit suite and `ruff check` pass.

This overlaps textually with #4221, which adds `and not self.low_confidence_filtered_count` right above the line I replace in `_prepare_review_finding_state`. The two conditions are independent, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

tickets.title: Chunked /review ignores num_max_findings, which also stops findings from being resolved
tickets.body:
### Git provider

Azure (the problem is in the provider-independent chunk merge, so other providers should behave the same)

### System Info

- pr-agent `main` at 330f0813 and v0.47.0, CLI in a CI container
- large-context model through LiteLLM
- `pr_reviewer.enable_large_pr_chunking = true`, `pr_reviewer.num_max_findings = 5`, `pr_reviewer.persistent_finding_state = true`

### Bug details

When `/review` is chunked, every chunk is allowed `num_max_findings` key issues, and `merge_review_chunks` unions them without applying the limit again (`key_issues_to_review: _union_of_lists(_key_issue_identity)` in `pr_agent/algo/review_merge.py`). A review of N chunks can therefore publish up to N x `num_max_findings` findings.

That has a second effect. `_prepare_review_finding_state` only lets a run resolve earlier findings when the run reported fewer findings than the limit:

```python
# pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py
and len(current_findings) < max_findings
```

After a chunked merge, the total is usually at or above the limit, so resolution is turned off for that run. On a large PR this happens on every run, which means:

- findings that a later commit fixed are never moved to `RESOLVED`, so the persistent review keeps listing them;
- since #3750 they are fed back to the model as `active` findings on every run;
- with `inline_key_issues`, the review publishes more inline threads than `num_max_findings` suggests.

**Reproduction** (on `main`):

```python
from pr_agent.algo.review_merge import merge_review_chunks

def issue(i, chunk):
    return {"relevant_file": f"src/chunk{chunk}/file{i}.py", "issue_header": f"Issue {chunk}.{i}",
            "issue_content": f"Problem {i} in chunk {chunk}", "start_line": 10, "end_line": 12}

# num_max_findings = 3, each chunk returns 3 findings
chunks = [{"review": {"key_issues_to_review": [issue(i, c) for i in range(3)]}} for c in (1, 2)]
print(len(merge_review_chunks(chunks)["review"]["key_issues_to_review"]))  # 6
```

**Expected:** a chunked review respects `num_max_findings` like a single-call review does, and the resolution guard means "this run may have left out a still-valid finding" rather than "the merged list is long".

**Possible directions:**

1. Base the resolution guard on the chunks: block resolution only when some chunk hit its own limit. That is the case the guard is there for, since only a full chunk can have left something out.
2. Cap the merged list at `num_max_findings`, and treat the findings that were cut as left out (not as absent), the same way `dropped_findings` already works.
3. Give each chunk a share of the limit instead of the full limit.

Option 1 alone fixes resolution. Option 2 or 3 also keeps the published count at the configured limit.

cases.title: fix(ignore): keep bracket expressions in string glob patterns
cases.description:
## Problem

`ignore.glob` accepts a list, but a string is a natural way to write one pattern or a short list. The string was split with `strip('[]').split(',')`.

`strip('[]')` removes every leading and trailing bracket, so a pattern that ends in a bracket expression loses its closing bracket. `split(',')` also cuts inside a bracket expression.

## Impact

```
ignore.glob = ["*.py[0-9]"]  -> ignored: gen.py1, gen.py2   (list form, correct)
ignore.glob = "*.py[0-9]"    -> ignored: nothing            (string form)
```

The excluded files still reach the model. The same happens for a comma inside a bracket expression, such as `file[1,2].txt`.

## Fix

A string value is split on top-level commas only, and one leading and one trailing bracket are removed as the list wrapper. A bracket expression keeps its brackets.

The list form is unchanged.

## Tests

Added to `tests/unittest/test_file_filter.py`:

- the string value splits into the expected patterns
- the string value ignores the matching files
- the string value and the list value ignore the same files

tickets.title: feat(jira): support scoped API tokens / service accounts via the Atlassian API gateway
tickets.body:
### Feature request

Add an optional `jira.cloud_id` setting. When it is set, Jira ticket-context lookups send API requests to the Atlassian platform gateway, `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<cloud_id>`, instead of `https://<jira_site>.atlassian.net`.

Proposed shape, keeping the fixed-destination design from #2420 and #4001:

- **Fixed host, validated value.** `cloud_id` must be a UUID, the same way `jira_site` must be a single DNS label. Requests can only ever go to `api.atlassian.com` or `<site>.atlassian.net`; nothing becomes a free-form URL.
- **Host-only.** It is added to `REPO_HOST_ONLY_KEYS_BY_SECTION["jira"]` next to `jira_site`, `jira_api_email` and `project_keys`. A repository's `.pr_agent.toml` and comment arguments cannot set it. It doesn't match the connection-key suffix rule, so it needs an explicit entry.
- **Fails closed.** A blank, non-string or non-UUID value turns off the Jira lookup with a warning that does not print the value, as an invalid `jira_site` does today.
- **API calls only.** The client uses the gateway, but ticket links stay `https://<jira_site>.atlassian.net/browse/KEY`. So `jira_site` remains required, and `add_jira_tickets()` still de-duplicates tickets by that link.
- **Same auth.** Basic auth with `jira_api_email` and `jira_api_token`, which Atlassian accepts on the gateway.
- **Opt-in.** With `cloud_id` unset, behavior is the same as today.

Out of scope: Jira Server / Data Center and arbitrary base URLs.

If this approach works for you, I'm happy to open a PR with:
- unit tests next to `TestJiraSiteInjection`, plus the host-only security tests
- updates to `fetching_ticket_context.md` and `configuration_options.md`
- the regenerated configuration reference

### Motivation

Jira ticket context (#2420) works only with classic, unscoped API tokens. Atlassian accepts **scoped** API tokens only through the platform gateway, and every service-account token is scoped. Atlassian's docs say: "Tokens must always use the Platform API Gateway URLs beginning with `api.atlassian.com`" ([docs](https://support.atlassian.com/user-management/docs/manage-api-tokens-for-service-accounts/)). On `<site>.atlassian.net`, such a token is treated as anonymous, so every lookup fails with:

```
Failed to fetch Jira ticket PROJ-123: Issue does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.
```

Atlassian tracks site-URL support for scoped tokens as an open suggestion ([JRACLOUD-94545](https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/JRACLOUD-94545), open since May 2025), so a fix on their side isn't coming soon.

This rules out the least-privilege setup. A ticket lookup only needs to read issues, but the only credential that works today is a classic token, which carries every permission of the user who created it, write and admin included. Teams that want a read-only (`read:jira-work`) token, or a dedicated service account that needs no Jira seat, can't use the feature. That matters most for a token stored in shared CI settings, which is exactly where a review bot's token ends up.

Verified with a service-account token (basic auth, `email:token`): `GET https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<cloudId>/rest/api/2/issue/PROJ-123` returns 200, while the same request to `https://<site>.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/PROJ-123` returns 404 with the error above.

`/config` prints every `[config]` and `pr_*` key not in its skip list (`pr_agent/tools/pr_config.py:66-78`), so host-only values such as `extra_config_url` (including any userinfo in the URL) and `global_settings_repo` appear in the PR thread for any commenter. `show_relevant_configurations` (`pr_agent/algo/run_output.py:101-132`) has a shorter skip list and no partial `key`/`secret`/`token` match, so a credential-like key under `[config]` would print its value.

cases.title: feat(cli): add a doctor command to preflight the deployment
cases.description:
## Problem

A misconfigured deployment only fails at the end of a full run. In the sample from #4195, 20 of 81 owners running the action publicly failed with `Incorrect API key provided: dummy_key`: the runner warns `OPENAI_KEY not set` and carries on, and every tool call then fails against the placeholder. Wrong base URLs and quota errors surface the same way, one full run later (#4320).

The existing `tests.health_test.main` needs a repository checkout (it is not shipped), a GitHub token, and real PRs — there is nothing lightweight to gate a setup with.

## Solution

`pr-agent doctor` — runs without `--pr_url` or a diff, never touches a git provider:

- `config.model` is set
- the active provider has a real key (env or settings — `_captured_api_key`, the same source a run uses; the value is never printed; providers unknown to the env table, i.e. keyless auth, defer to the ping)
- a one-token completion against the configured model succeeds, through the real `LiteLLMAIHandler.chat_completion` path

One line per check on stdout; exit code 0 only when everything passes, so CI setups can gate on it. No new settings; no existing command changes (`doctor` joins only the CLI choices, not the agent dispatch).

## Testing

- Passing setup → all three checks pass, exit 0; missing key names the env variable, placeholder key fails, bad ping reports the failure reason — each exits 1.
- `doctor` never constructs `PRAgent` (asserted), and the key value never appears in the output.
- CLI regression suite (201 tests) and ruff pass.

Fixes #4320

tickets.title: docs: add "Incorrect API key provided: dummy_key" to the GitHub Action troubleshooting list
tickets.body:
When the action runs without an OpenAI key, the runner prints "OPENAI_KEY not set" (`pr_agent/servers/github_action_runner.py:226-230`) and carries on. With the default OpenAI model, every tool then sends pr-agent's placeholder key (`DUMMY_LITELLM_API_KEY`, `pr_agent/algo/ai_handlers/cloud_auth.py:77`) and fails with "Incorrect API key provided: dummy_key". The "Common Error Messages and Solutions" list in `docs/docs/installation/github.md` covers "API key not found", which is not what this failure prints.

In a sample of failed runs from 81 owners using the action publicly over the last 14 days, 20 failed this way. 18 passed their OpenAI key variable empty: 5 on Dependabot PRs and 2 on fork PRs, which get no Actions secrets on `pull_request`, and 11 most likely with an unset or misnamed secret. The other 2 had another provider's key variables but left `config.model` at the OpenAI default.

Suggested change: an entry for that exact message covering the three causes: a PR event that gets no secrets (see the `pull_request_target` section, the `sender.type != 'Bot'` guard in the basic example, or Dependabot secrets), a missing or misnamed secret, and another provider's key with the default model. Optionally, the runner's "OPENAI_KEY not set" line could check the key pr-agent will actually use: it also prints when the key arrives as `OPENAI__KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`, which both work.

cases.title: fix(improve): retry unusable self-reflection feedback
cases.description:
## Problem

The `/improve` tool stops its self-reflection fallback chain at the first non-empty model response, even when the parsed feedback cannot be used. Missing score data or required line anchors can cause generated suggestions to be dropped instead of trying an available fallback model.

## Change

- Parse reflection feedback before accepting it, and try the next configured reasoning model when no usable feedback is present.
- Require usable line anchors for positive scores if the original suggestion has none, while retaining valid zero-score rejections and partially usable feedback.
- Reuse the original suggestions, respect existing model and deployment restrictions, and avoid reparsing accepted YAML.
- Explain fallback behavior and potential additional model usage in the documentation.

## Tests

Cover malformed feedback, missing or invalid anchors, zero scores, partial feedback, model order, pinned deployments, and recovering suggestions without regenerating them.

cases.description:
## What / Why / How

Static AWS credentials are now used as a fallback only for authentication and permission errors. Bedrock service errors and timeouts keep using IMDS credentials during retries, so transient failures do not change the credential source for later calls. Fixes #4413.

## Affected platforms

PR-Agent's AWS Bedrock backend when IMDS credentials are enabled.

## Test plan

`PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest tests/unittest/test_litellm_imds.py -q` (268 passed); Ruff and pre-commit passed.

tickets.title: AWS_USE_IMDS: a Bedrock 503 or timeout permanently switches the handler to the static credentials
tickets.body:
With `AWS_USE_IMDS=true` and static `[aws]` keys configured, the `except openai.APIError` branch in `_chat_completion_with_retry` (`pr_agent/algo/ai_handlers/litellm_ai_handler.py:3240`) calls `_activate_static_aws_fallback()` for every error except a rate limit, not only for credential failures. A Bedrock 503 `ServiceUnavailableException` is therefore re-sent at once with the static keys, and `_aws_imds_fell_back` stays `True`, so every later call from that handler uses the static keys. #2307 described the fallback as "if the ambient credentials fail a Bedrock call". The immediate re-send also bypasses the same-model backoff proposed in #4407.

Verified on main (5eaa1265a) with the fixtures in `tests/unittest/test_litellm_imds.py`: a `litellm.ServiceUnavailableError` followed by a success gives two calls, `IMDS-KEY` then `STATIC-KEY`, and leaves `_aws_imds_fell_back` set to `True`. `test_chat_completion_preserves_static_fallback_for_api_errors` (line 2143) pins the same behaviour for `APITimeoutError`.

Suggested fix: switch only on errors that can mean the ambient credentials are wrong (`AuthenticationError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, plus the refresh failures `_snapshot_aws_request_credentials` already handles), and let capacity errors and timeouts go through the normal retry. The timeout case in that test would then expect no switch.

cases.title: fix(servers): disable_auto_feedback stops push and review commands too
cases.description:
Fixes #4448

## What

With `config.disable_auto_feedback = true` the docs promise that no automatic tool runs when a PR is opened or new code is pushed. Only the Bitbucket Server webhook did that. The other runners checked the flag only for `pr_commands` (the GitHub App also for `review_commands`), so `push_commands` still ran, and so did GitLab's `reviewer_commands`.

- New `auto_feedback_disabled()` in `pr_agent/servers/utils.py`: the one predicate for the flag.
- The GitHub App, GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps Server runners call it before running any auto command. Their existing log messages and early-return behaviour stay as they were. Bitbucket Server already gated every command and is unchanged.

## Tests

New `tests/unittest/test_disable_auto_feedback_servers.py` (13 tests): for each of those five runners and every command list it can be asked to run (pr / push / review / reviewer commands), a recording agent is given `/review` as the configured command with the flag on, and no command may run. 4 of the 13 fail without the server changes (`push_commands` on the GitHub App, Gitea, Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps Server) and all 13 pass with them.

I also ran the existing server-related tests (`-k` on github_app, gitlab, gitea, bitbucket, azure_devops, push_trigger, auto_feedback) before and after: 29 failed / 2258 passed in both runs, with the identical failures. Those failures come from my local environment (missing optional extras), not from this change, so CI is the real check.

Not covered: I did not run the Bitbucket Server webhook in the new test since it already honoured the flag. GitLab's reviewer_commands is now also gated; if you would rather keep reviewer assignment independent of the flag, say so and I will drop that.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

cases.title: fix(providers): validate suggestion line ranges in Gerrit, Gitea and CodeCommit
cases.description:
Fixes #4514.

`_is_valid_code_suggestion` now rejects any start line below 1. It used to accept negative starts other than -1, such as -5 to -3. Gerrit, Gitea and CodeCommit now run the check before publishing.

- **Gerrit** is the provider where an inverted range does real damage: `add_suggestion` writes `lines[:start-1]`, then the suggestion, then `lines[end:]`, so a 5-to-3 range kept every original line and repeated line 4. Inverted ranges are now skipped before the file is touched.
- **Gitea and CodeCommit** anchor on the start line only. A start below 1 cannot anchor a comment, and an inverted range means the suggestion is malformed, so both now skip what the inherited base `publish_code_suggestions` already skips for GitHub and Bitbucket.
- **Local and plain diff** only render the range into a markdown file, so they are unchanged and still show whatever the model returned.
- The check reads both keys with `.get()`. A Gitea or CodeCommit suggestion without `relevant_lines_end` is still checked on its start line alone, as before.

tickets.title: Gerrit repeats lines on an inverted suggestion range; four other overrides skip the check too
tickets.body:
Since #3726 the base `publish_code_suggestions` (git_provider.py:680) rejects a suggestion whose end line is before its start (`_is_valid_code_suggestion`, :708-722). GitHub and both Bitbuckets inherit it, and Azure and GitLab have their own checks. Five overrides have none: Gitea (gitea_provider.py:489), CodeCommit (codecommit_provider.py:341), Gerrit (gerrit_provider.py:485), Local (local_git_provider.py:164) and Plain diff (plain_diff_provider.py:205).

Only Gerrit uses the end line to rewrite the file: `add_suggestion` (gerrit_provider.py:203) writes `lines[:start-1]`, the suggestion, then `lines[end:]`, so a range of 5 to 3 keeps every original line and repeats line 4. Gitea and CodeCommit anchor on the start line only, and Local and Plain diff only print the range. Checked on main (d3b606a7e).

Suggested change: tighten `_is_valid_code_suggestion` to reject any start below 1 (it accepts -5 to -3 today), call it in Gerrit with a test, and in the other four if an inverted range should be dropped there too. CodeCommit and Gitea need `.get()`-safe handling of a missing `relevant_lines_end`.

Done when the check rejects starts below 1, Gerrit skips an inverted range, and the other four are decided.

cases.title: fix(gitlab): skip webhook events from ignored user IDs
cases.description:
Fixes #4561

The GitLab webhook only skips bots by display name (`config.bot_user_indicators`). Display names are free text, so "Jane Abbot-Smith" is skipped while "Renovate Bot" is not. GitLab already sends the sender's numeric `user.id` on merge request and note events, and that ID is stable.

## Changes
- New `gitlab.ignore_user_ids = []` in `[gitlab]`. `is_bot_user` checks `str(user.id)` against it before the name check.
- It takes a list, a single int (`GITLAB__IGNORE_USER_IDS=123`) or a single string. Entries are normalised with `str(x).strip()`, and a missing `user.id` never matches.
- `bot_user_indicators` is unchanged. An unlisted ID falls through to the name check.
- The `configuration.toml` comment says the key is host-only, because the check runs before repository settings are loaded. `configuration_reference.md` is regenerated with `scripts/generate_config_reference.py`, and the active-key count in `test_config_reference.py` goes from 306 to 307.
- Sibling providers: the GitHub App uses the sender `type == "Bot"` and Bitbucket uses the actor type. Neither matches on names, so they are not changed here.

## Tests
New cases in `tests/unittest/test_webhook_logic_core.py`: listed and unlisted IDs, int and string entries, padded strings, a single scalar int or string, a missing `user.id`, an empty list, and a listed ID skipped whatever the display name. 6 of them fail on `main`.

tickets.title: GitHub Action runner runs auto tools twice for PRs created with a requested reviewer (no first-open guard, unlike the App path)
tickets.body:
### What happened?

The GitHub Action runner path runs the enabled auto tools **twice** for PRs that are created with a requested reviewer.

- The runner's default `PR_ACTIONS` includes `review_requested` (`pr_agent/servers/github_action_runner.py:393-396`), and the dispatch check (`:445`) only tests `action in pr_actions` — there is no first-open guard.
- The GitHub App path guards the same event stream: `github_app.py:474-477` skips `review_requested` when `pull_request.created_at == pull_request.updated_at`, with the comment *"avoid double reviews when opening a PR for the first time"* — and that guard is pinned by `tests/unittest/test_github_app_timeout_core.py::test_rejects_synchronize_when_created_equals_updated`.
- The two entries even disagree in `configuration.toml`: the App-side default (`:360`) omits `review_requested`, while the Action-side comment example (`:346`) includes it. The official install workflow from the docs (`docs/docs/installation/github.md:73`) also lists `review_requested` in `types:`.

When a PR is created with a reviewer selected, GitHub dispatches both `pull_request.opened` and `pull_request.review_requested`. Both pass the runner's check, so `_run_auto_tool` executes the enabled tools (describe + review + improve) twice — double the model calls on the operator's key, and two concurrent runs racing on the same persistent comment heads.

### Steps to Reproduce

Unit-level (mirrors `test_run_action_invokes_enabled_auto_tools_for_pull_request_event` in `tests/unittest/test_github_action_runner_core.py`): set `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=pull_request`, payload `action: "review_requested"` with `created_at == updated_at`, keep the default `pr_actions`. The runner invokes the same tool set as an `opened` event — i.e. the suite runs for the first-open event stream that the App path suppresses.

Repo-level: install with the default workflow from the docs, create a PR with a reviewer pre-selected, and observe two full auto-tool runs.

### Expected Behavior

The Action path should mirror the App guard: skip `review_requested` when `created_at == updated_at` (first open), so the same event stream produces one run regardless of entry point.

### Environment

- Operating System: n/a (workflow configuration logic, not runtime-specific)
- Installation Method: GitHub Action (default `pr-agent-review.yaml` from the docs)
- Agent Canvas Version: n/a — observed on `pr-agent` main @ `e7c6dfb`

cases.title: fix(azure): preserve physical lines in suggestion ranges and reconciliation
cases.description:
Azure DevOps suggestion positions and reconciliation count lines with `splitlines()`, which treats U+2028, NEL, form feed and similar characters as line breaks. A separator before the anchor makes the final UTF-16 column come from a different physical line. During reconciliation, one physical line containing a non-LF separator can also compare equal to a two-line suggestion and incorrectly mark an unapplied thread fixed.

Use the shared Git/LF-aware splitter for final-line offsets, fetched file content and proposed code. Add regressions for the offset, an applied suggestion after a separator, and an unapplied multiline suggestion that previously compared equal. This addresses Azure publication/reconciliation, separately from supplied-diff parsing.
