cases.description: ## Problem `extract_ticket_links_from_pr_description()` filters out closed HTML comments (``), certain link-text `#N` tokens, Tailwind arbitrary values such as `bg-[#121212]`, and bare `#N` tokens longer than `MAX_SHORTHAND_ISSUE_DIGITS` (6 digits). However, `extract_gitlab_ticket_references()` in the same module still matched those patterns as local issue references in the current GitLab project and passed unvalidated `issue_iid` strings directly to `int()`. ## Change - Skip GitLab ticket references inside closed HTML comments (`_html_comment_spans()`). - For bare `#N` matches outside HTML comments, lazily compute `_non_reference_hash_starts(pr_description, ())` and skip tokens matched by `_is_non_reference_hash()` (including `#N` forming the entire link text of `[#N](...)`, `[#N][ref]`, or `#N`, hashes glued to word characters, and `bg-[#121212]`-style Tailwind arbitrary values). - Apply `MAX_SHORTHAND_ISSUE_DIGITS` (6 digits) to bare `#N` references in `extract_gitlab_ticket_references()`, validate extracted `issue_iid` strings as positive ASCII integers, and guard `int()` conversion against `ValueError`. - Update `docs/docs/core-abilities/fetching_ticket_context.md` to note that built-in matching on both GitHub and GitLab recognizes local `#` references of up to six digits. - Compatibility note: bare `#N` tokens longer than 6 characters (such as `#1234567` or zero-padded `#0000042`) are no longer treated as local GitLab issue references; explicit `group/proj#1234567` references and full GitLab issue URLs remain supported. ## Testing - Expanded parameterized test cases in `tests/unittest/test_ticket_extraction_async.py` (`TestGitLabExtraction.test_shorthand_reference_boundaries`) covering 6- and 7-digit bare `#N` boundaries, closed HTML comments, Markdown/HTML `#N` link text, Tailwind arbitrary values, `#0`, non-ASCII digits, and oversized integers.

cases.title: fix(bitbucket): decode each file of the PR diff on its own
cases.description:
`BitbucketProvider.get_diff_files` reads the PR diff with atlassian's `PullRequest.diff()`, which decodes the whole response as UTF-8. The pull request diff redirects to the [repository diff](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-commits/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-diff-spec-get), whose reference says: "The raw diff is returned as-is, in whatever encoding the files in the repository use. It is not decoded into unicode." So one file that is not UTF-8, such as a Java `.properties` file kept in ISO-8859-1 or a cp1252 source file, makes that raise `UnicodeDecodeError`. The fallback then re-reads the diff with the first of `['iso-8859-1', 'latin-1', 'ascii', 'utf-16']`. ISO-8859-1 cannot fail, so the whole diff is decoded as Latin-1, the other entries are never tried, and every non-ASCII character of every UTF-8 file in the PR reaches `/review`, `/describe` and `/improve` as mojibake. The fallback catches every exception, so a first request that fails for another reason, such as a connection reset, garbles an all-UTF-8 diff the same way, under a "Failed to decode PR patch with utf-8" warning.

#4648 fixed the raw file reads and called the diff right, which holds only while every file in the PR is UTF-8. The base file now decodes as UTF-8, so a hunk that opens with a garbled line no longer matches it and also loses its extra context.

## Before / after

A PR with a UTF-8 `src/greeting.py` and an ISO-8859-1 `messages_de.properties`. `pr.diff()` is atlassian's own `PullRequest.diff()` on those bytes, and `extend_patch` runs with the default 5 lines before and 1 after (script below). On `main` (eac9d734f) the log says `Invalid hunk in PR, line 7 in hunk header doesn't match the original file content`, and `greeting.py` comes out as (`\x` escapes stand for control and no-break characters):

```text
@@ -7,7 +7,7 @@
     # GrÃ¼Ã\x9fe aus KÃ¶ln â\x80\x93 ä½\xa0å¥½
     greeting = f'Hallo {NAME}'
     print(greeting)
-    print('cafÃ©')
+    print('cafÃ© â\x98\x95')
     return 0
 
 
```

With this change:

```text
@@ -2,13 +2,13 @@
 
 NAME = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'Welt'
 
 
 def main():
     # Grüße aus Köln – 你好
     greeting = f'Hallo {NAME}'
     print(greeting)
-    print('café')
+    print('café ☕')
     return 0
 
 
 if __name__ == '__main__':
```

The `.properties` file decodes the same on both: `+greeting=Schöne Grüße`.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# PYTHONPATH=. uv run python repro.py
import difflib
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from atlassian.bitbucket.cloud.repositories.pullRequests import PullRequest

from pr_agent.algo.git_patch_processing import decode_if_bytes, extend_patch
from pr_agent.git_providers.bitbucket_provider import BitbucketProvider

BASE = ("import sys\n\nNAME = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'Welt'\n\n\ndef main():\n"
        "    # Grüße aus Köln – 你好\n    greeting = f'Hallo {NAME}'\n    print(greeting)\n"
        "    print('café')\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    sys.exit(main())\n")
FILES = {  # path: (base, head, encoding of the file in the repository)
    "src/greeting.py": (BASE, BASE.replace("print('café')", "print('café ☕')"), "utf-8"),
    "src/main/resources/messages_de.properties": (
        "app.title=Anwendung\ngreeting=Grüße\n", "app.title=Anwendung\ngreeting=Schöne Grüße\n", "iso-8859-1"),
}
raw_diff = b"".join(
    (f"diff --git a/{path} b/{path}\n" + "".join(difflib.unified_diff(
        base.splitlines(True), head.splitlines(True), f"a/{path}", f"b/{path}"))).encode(encoding)
    for path, (base, head, encoding) in FILES.items())

provider = BitbucketProvider.__new__(BitbucketProvider)
provider.diff_files, provider.pr = None, MagicMock()
diffstats = []
for path in FILES:
    diffstat = MagicMock()
    diffstat.new.path = diffstat.old.path = path
    diffstat.data = {"status": "modified", "lines_added": 1, "lines_removed": 1}
    diffstat.old.get_data.return_value = diffstat.new.get_data.return_value = None
    diffstats.append(diffstat)
provider.pr.diffstat.return_value = diffstats
api = MagicMock()
api.get.return_value = raw_diff  # atlassian's own PullRequest.diff() decodes these bytes
provider.pr.diff.side_effect = lambda encoding="utf-8": PullRequest.diff(api, encoding=encoding)

for file in provider.get_diff_files():
    # File contents decoded as _get_pr_file_content decodes them since #4648.
    base, head = (decode_if_bytes(text.encode(FILES[file.filename][2])) for text in FILES[file.filename][:2])
    print(f"## {file.filename}{extend_patch(base, file.patch, 5, 1, file.filename, new_file_str=head)}")
```

</details>

## Change

The UTF-8 read is unchanged, so a diff that decodes still takes one request. The fallback reads the diff once as ISO-8859-1, which maps every byte to one character, splits it at the `diff --git` headers as before, and decodes each file's part with `decode_if_bytes`, as `_get_pr_file_content` decodes file contents: UTF-8 when that part is valid UTF-8, else Latin-1. The unreachable encodings and the `ValueError` after them are gone, and the warning names the exception type.

## Sibling providers

GitHub and GitLab get one patch per file in JSON, Azure DevOps and Bitbucket Server build each patch from that file's contents, and CodeCommit, Gerrit and local git skip or flag a file that is not UTF-8. Gitea also splits one aggregate `.diff`, but decodes it with `errors="replace"`: its other files stay intact and only the undecodable bytes of the non-UTF-8 file become U+FFFD, as `test_gitea_provider_decodes_non_utf8_diff_with_replacement` pins. I left it as it is.

## Not changed

- A file whose part of the diff is not valid UTF-8 still decodes as Latin-1, as today and as its contents do: right for ISO-8859-1, while cp1252-only characters such as `€` or curly quotes come out as C1 control characters.
- The fallback still runs after any exception and makes one more request, as before.

## Testing

- `test_bitbucket_provider.py`, with `pr.diff` answering like atlassian (`str(raw, encoding)`): a diff with a UTF-8 file and an ISO-8859-1 `.properties` file keeps `café ☕` and `你好` and decodes `Schöne Grüße`, with the same two requests as before; a diff whose first request raises `ConnectionError` keeps its UTF-8 text. Both fail on `main` and pass with the change.
- That file plus `test_bitbucket_diff_line_counts.py`, `test_bitbucket_inline_comment_dedup.py` and `test_provider_http_timeout.py`: 324 passed on `main`, 326 with the change, 4 skipped on both. The 34 test files that mention `BitbucketProvider`, `bitbucket_provider`, `extend_patch` or `git_patch_processing`: 1865 and 1867 passed, with the same 5 failures on both in my environment (Windows, Python 3.12, `PYTHONUTF8=1`: CRLF in `test_local_git_provider.py`, a subprocess import in `test_silent_failure_fallbacks.py`).
- `ruff check` (0.17.4, with the new PERF rules) and `uvx pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: clean (actionlint skipped, no workflow changes).

Not tested against a live Bitbucket Cloud workspace: the diff bytes are canned and decoded by atlassian-python-api's own `PullRequest.diff()` (5.0.5).

cases.title: feat(gitlab): include discussion history in inline /ask
cases.description:
## Motivation

GitLab inline `/ask` replies are posted in the selected diff discussion, but follow-up questions currently lack earlier messages from that thread. GitHub and Azure DevOps already provide same-thread context for line questions.

## Changes

- Read earlier notes from the selected GitLab discussion using the existing line-question history path.
- Pass the triggering note ID separately from the discussion ID used for replies. Exclude the current question, later replies, system notes, and empty notes.
- When the origin note is missing or discussion history cannot be read, answer the current question independently.
- Reuse the existing `pr_questions.use_conversation_history` option, shared input-token budget, and untrusted-discussion guidance.
- Update the Ask documentation.

## Scope and compatibility

- Applies only to GitLab inline `/ask` on diff lines; top-level `/ask`, reply placement, and thread resolution are unchanged.
- With history enabled (the default), each eligible question adds one GitLab discussion API read and may consume additional input tokens, without another model request.
- Set `pr_questions.use_conversation_history=false` to disable the additional read.
- No new dependencies or configuration keys.
